_meta.how_to_regress: npm run check:golden drive-home  (dev backend up)
_meta.note: V2 rewrite, 2026-08-25. Replaces the v1 sample outright: the old tool ran web_search and spoke confidently about named highways and interchanges it could not see, which is the failure this version exists to remove. The shape changed with it — safety_overview, risk_level, honest_assessment, checklist and before_you_go are gone, and there is no risk score of any kind. The endpoint takes enum ids now (time_of_day, road_type, driver_state, conditions[]), not display labels. driver_state "very_tired" is a SERVER-SIDE boundary: case 4 returns do_not_drive from a localized string table without calling the model, so it must stay byte-stable and must never contain English. Case 3 is the German stress case (four conditions plus a long concern) and guards against truncation. Case 3 uses driver_state "fine" deliberately: on an "a_little_tired" run factors_in_favor is often legitimately empty — the prompt forbids inventing one — and pinning it non-empty made this check flap. router.outputGuard is live, so expect "v2 guard: FAIL (n field(s))" in the log on the pause cases; that is the guard catching route_fact_from_place_names and repairing it, not an error.

input.concern: It is much later than I meant to stay out.

output.headline: Nothing in what you reported gives a clear reason to wait — proceeding appears reasonable.
output.summary: You report feeling fine, conditions are clear, and the drive is a short 20 minutes on city streets. The only hesitation you noted is the late hour, which is worth keeping in mind but is not itself a reason to hold off.
output.main_concern: Late-night driving can bring more fatigue and fewer other road users to notice hazards — worth staying attentive even on a short trip.
factors_harder: Late hour means fewer witnesses to hazards and a higher chance you will encounter someone else whose judgment is affected by fatigue or impairment
Later than you planned to stay — quick self-check before starting makes sense
factors_in_favor: City streets — familiar enough that you know the general area
output.before_you_decide: Take 30 seconds before you start the car. If you notice eye heaviness, slow reactions, or difficulty focusing, that is a signal to pause and reassess rather than begin the drive.
prep_checklist: Do a quick honest self-check — eyes alert, reactions feeling normal
Phone silenced or in do-not-disturb before you pull out
Doors locked, mirrors set before moving
Let someone know you are heading home if that feels right
Keep music or radio at a level that helps you stay alert without being distracting
watch_for: Feeling your eyes getting heavy or needing to blink hard to focus
How you handle steering corrections and how quickly you respond to traffic lights
Any sign that other drivers are behaving erratically — give extra space
If anything feels off mid-drive, pulling over in a well-lit spot is always an option
limits: Drive Home is not a live traffic, weather, or road-condition service.
This assessment uses only the conditions you reported.

input.concern: I have not driven in snow since last winter and I do not know how the pass looks.

output.headline: Hold off until you know what the pass looks like — that gap matters before you commit to a highway drive in snow and wind.
output.summary: You have reported snow or ice, high wind, and a 90-minute highway drive in early morning darkness. You have also flagged that you do not know current conditions on the pass, which is the one piece of information most likely to change this call.
output.main_concern: You do not know the pass conditions, and that gap is too significant to ignore before starting a winter highway drive.
factors_harder: Snow or ice reported on a highway route
High wind reported, which can reduce visibility and affect vehicle stability
Early morning timing means reduced visibility for the next few hours
Self-reported rustiness driving in snow since last winter
factors_in_favor: You recognized the uncertainty before starting — that awareness is itself useful
You recognized the gap in what you know before starting — that awareness is itself useful
output.before_you_decide: Check the current road and pass conditions through your state DOT road conditions service before deciding anything else — if the pass is closed, restricted to certain vehicles, or rated poor, that changes the call entirely.
safer_options: Check CDOT road conditions (cotrip.org) and WYDOT (wyoroad.info) for current pass status before leaving
Check current conditions and decide based on what the road conditions services report, not on when daylight arrives
Call your parents and agree on a decision window — leave by X or postpone
Consider delaying the trip by a few hours and reassessing conditions mid-morning
If the visit is flexible, travel tomorrow if conditions are forecast to improve
watch_for: Blowing snow or whiteout reducing visibility to unsafe levels
Ice patches causing loss of traction, especially on bridges and overpasses
Strong crosswind gusts making the vehicle hard to hold in lane
Any sign of increasing fatigue or anxiety that affects your focus
limits: Drive Home is not a live traffic, weather, or road-condition service.
This assessment uses only the conditions you reported.

input.concern: Die Sicht wird schlechter und ich kenne die Umleitung durch die Baustelle nicht.

output.headline: Kurze Pause empfohlen – unbekannte Umleitung bei schlechter Sicht klärt sich besser vor der Abfahrt.
output.summary: Du fühlst dich nach eigener Einschätzung gut, aber Regen, Nebel und eine dir unbekannte Baustellenumleitung zur späten Stunde sind zusammen eine schwierige Konstellation. Die Umleitungsstrecke kurz nachzuvollziehen, bevor du losfährst, bringt dir Sicherheit.
output.main_concern: Unbekannte Umleitung bei schlechter Sicht – bevor du startest, solltest du die Route kurz nachvollziehen, damit die Unsicherheit geringer wird.
factors_harder: Regen und Nebel mit sich weiter verschlechternder Sicht
factors_in_favor: Fahrer fühlt sich nach eigener Einschätzung gut
output.before_you_decide: Schau dir die Umleitungsführung durch die Baustelle kurz an einem Navigationsgerät oder einer Karten-App an, bevor du startest – wenn du die Strecke grob kennst, fällt die Unsicherheit bei schlechter Sicht deutlich geringer aus.
safer_options: Umleitungsroute jetzt am Gerät oder Telefon nachvollziehen, dann neu bewerten
Kurz warten und prüfen, ob sich Nebel oder Verkehr bessern
Taxi oder Ridesharing-Dienst für diese Nacht nutzen
Öffentliche Verkehrsmittel prüfen, falls noch verfügbar
Warten und prüfen, ob sich Nebel oder Verkehr bessern
watch_for: Sicht verschlechtert sich so stark, dass Fahrbahnrand oder Gegenverkehr kaum noch erkennbar sind
Orientierungsverlust oder Unsicherheit an der Umleitung
Starke Verkehrsstauungen, die eine Umplanung sinnvoll machen
limits: Drive Home ist kein Live-Dienst für Verkehr, Wetter oder Straßenzustand.
Diese Einschätzung verwendet nur die von dir gemeldeten Bedingungen.

output.headline: Fahre jetzt nicht los, wenn du sehr müde bist.
output.summary: Die wichtigste Information ist deine aktuelle Müdigkeit. Verschiebe die Fahrt oder nutze eine andere Möglichkeit, nach Hause zu kommen, statt mit starker Müdigkeit zu fahren.
output.main_concern: Du hast angegeben, sehr müde zu sein.
output.before_you_decide: Bewerte die Fahrt erst neu, wenn du wirklich ausgeruht bist und Wachbleiben und Konzentration kein Problem mehr sind.
safer_options: Warte und ruhe dich aus, bevor du die Fahrt neu bewertest.
Bleib dort, wenn das praktikabel ist.
Bitte eine ausgeruhte Person zu fahren.
Nutze Taxi, Fahrdienst, öffentliche Verkehrsmittel oder eine andere verfügbare Alternative.
limits: Drive Home ist kein Live-Dienst für Verkehr, Wetter oder Straßenzustand.
Diese Einschätzung verwendet nur die von dir gemeldeten Bedingungen.
